title: 43% of Workers Would Take a Pay Cut to Go Freelance
paragraphs: Which do you prefer? The stability and regular pay of a nine-to-five job, or the freedom and opportunity of freelance work?

If you're a full-time worker thinking about going freelance, you're far from alone. Sharon Steiner from Fiverr, a platform for freelance workers, recently said the company's data had found that 77% of full-time workers are interested in moving to freelance work. In fact, 67% even say they think they'll make freelancing their main job in the next three years.

Fiverr also commissioned Talker Research to survey almost 5,800 full-time workers and freelancers in the US, the UK, Canada, Germany and Australia. The survey found that not only are many full-time workers interested in freelancing, but 43% would take a pay cut if it meant they could be their own boss.

Many full-time workers say they're actually already working a little like freelancers. And it's not just having more flexible hours and doing more meetings over video — some full-time workers are even being paid per project instead of getting a regular salary.

It also looks like workers in general are less interested in nine-to-five jobs, with 51% of all workers saying a perfect workday actually starts before 9 a.m. — and 42% saying it should end before 5 p.m.
So it sounds like, for many, freelancing may be the answer. But is the picture really so rosy?

Well, the Talker Research survey found that, on an average day, freelancers do have fewer meetings than full-time workers. However, they also work two hours longer each week. And freelancers have problems getting respect, with 29% saying they wish freelancing was seen as a real job, not just "side work."
So it's not all upsides. The choice really depends on what's most important for you.
